answer: An agent network trading raven telemetry, trellis data, and relic logs can curb Sybils using TPM Direct Anonymous Attestation. Each agent signs its public key with a zero-knowledge credential from a chip-fused endorsement key tied to an epoch basename, yielding a deterministic per-chip pseudonym verified against vendor root certificates. Each fake identity thus requires a distinct physical TPM. Yet attackers renting bare-metal nodes or extracting flawed-silicon keys can still run bulk Sybils.
